# PCA Project Highlights — Dopamine/GABA Stimulus Reward Learning

This document summarizes the strongest findings and the best plots from the current branch.



## 1. Most informative visual assets (generated files)
- `outputs/SpontFB/GABA/SpontFB_GABA_trajectory.png`
- `outputs/ToneFB/GABA/ToneFB_GABA_trajectory.png`
- `outputs/ToneFB/Dopamine/ToneFB_Dopamine_trajectory.png`

## 2. Key behavioral insights
- GABA trajectories provide better low-dimensional separation than dopamine in cross-group comparisons (see GABA PC1/PC2 clusters).
- ToneFB signals are consistently more structured than CRFB and SpontFB in PC subspaces, suggesting stronger stimulus-locked dynamics.


## 3. Crossing conditions worth presenting
- `outputs/cross_dataset/CRFB_to_ToneFB/` and `outputs/cross_dataset/ToneFB_to_CRFB/` overlays (cross-session alignment quality) 
- `outputs/overlays/CRFB_vs_ToneFB_Dopamine_overlay.html` and `ToneFB_vs_CRFB_GABA_overlay.html`
- `outputs/diagnostics/CRFB_Dopamine_sep_diagnostic.html` and `ToneFB_Dopamine_sep_diagnostic.html`

## 4. Notebooks to show results
- `PCA_Framework.ipynb` (framework pipeline + plots)
- `PCA_Advanced_Analysis.ipynb` (detailed model comparisons + higher-order analysis)
- `Plots PCA - trajectories & overlay .ipynb` (final range of trajectory overlays + custom figure assembly)
